units.summary: verify-peer-dependencies incompatible-peer-range: a declared peer range is compatible with what the dependency requires

changes.why: Moderate confidence. Stage A says the check reads the installed dependencies, but getDependencyManifest (verify-peer-dependencies/index.ts) reads workspace dependencies from the tree, meaning the committed manifests. It reads node_modules only for external ones, and it skips an unresolvable dependency instead of reporting it. At fluentui, the forwarding chains are mostly workspace-internal: react-button depends on react-aria, react-tabster and others, which all declare react and @types/react peers. The code itself calls the check 'version math, not resolution mechanics'. The assertion is that the declared peer range is a subset of each workspace dependency's required peer range. It needs a semver-range subset operator plus a name-to-manifest join (needs: entry-values), so it is B-adapter (reference). If the integrator prefers, split off the external-dependency half as D.

stage_b_config_issues: fluentui-02 / microsoft-fluentui-yarnpath-resolves does not fire when the yarnPath key is deleted. registry_paths_resolve is silent on an absent field, as rules.md documents. A yaml_path_matches on $.yarnPath, for example '^\.yarn/releases/yarn-[^/]+\.cjs$', would close the gap.

microsoft-fluentui-export-maps-entry-fields has the wrong scope. It includes packages/react-components/react-jsx-runtime/package.json, which is type module and not private but tagged vNext + platform:any, and export-maps-sync skips it (REQUIRED_TAGS is vNext and platform:web). The rule covers 82 manifests, not the 81 its comment and fluentui-11 claim. It would false-fire if react-jsx-runtime changed its entry fields.

microsoft-fluentui-react-components-unstable-api-frozen does not express its unit (R4). The digest forbids the react-virtualizer additions that src/unstable/index.ts:5 explicitly allows, and any cosmetic api-extractor change. See the reclassify of fluentui-14 to C.

microsoft-fluentui-peer-ranges-valid-semver is broader than invalid-peer-range in two ways its comment does not mention. The generator skips private packages and NON_SEMVER_RANGE protocol ranges (workspace:, portal:, link:, file:, npm:, patch:; index.ts:100 and :519-521), so the rule would false-fire on an npm: alias peer range or a private package's range. Its evidence cites index.ts:320, which is getUnverifiedFloor (the opt-in unverified-peer-range). The invalid-peer-range check is in getManifestViolations, index.ts:510-529.

microsoft-fluentui-api-reports-lf: .gitattributes:5 is `*.api.md text=auto` with no eol=lf. Git normalizes only the committed blob, and alint reads the working tree. A Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true has CRLF api.md files, and this rule would fire although the repository content is LF. It passes on the Linux clone. The jest-19 precedent had eol=lf.

microsoft-fluentui-no-tslint-comments is a text regex, not comment-token aware. It fires on `/// tslint:disable`, where ESLint's comment.value '/ tslint...' does not match ^\s*tslint. It also fires on the directive inside string literals outside packages/eslint-plugin. It passes at the pin, which is acceptable under the batch-2 ruling.

microsoft-fluentui-syncpack-is-root-devdependency and -beachball-is-root-devdependency use '^\S+$', which fires on an empty string that the github-script guard (typeof === 'string') accepts. This is slightly stricter than the gate, and the difference is negligible.

stage_b_summary:
I found 19 enforced behaviors that Stage A missed. Most are bespoke Jest tests and load-bearing comments that Stage A either folded into "tests pass" (fluentui-38, D) or skipped, against R7 and its own standard for fluentui-04 and fluentui-15.

**Missed units:**
- **Azure corepack ban (toolchain-pin, A, fired).** tools.yml:44-45 says never to run `corepack enable`.
- **Change-file comment prefix (other, A).** dev-workflow.md:95 asks for feat:/fix:/chore:/docs:/refactor:.
- **Three more load-bearing comments (other, A):**
  - the Nx markers in AGENTS.md;
  - the copilot-setup-steps job name;
  - dependabot's production `allow` entry.
- **The react-icons-mdl2 *Icon.tsx file-name test (other, A).**
- **Eight units from apps/public-docsite-v9's migrationGuides.test.ts:**
  - A: the ColorMapping header, the storySort order, inline TSX in the added guides, and no empty code fences;
  - C: guide structure, because a fence-blind one-H1 regex false-fires on Icon.mdx at the pin;
  - B-config unique-key: unique Storybook routes;
  - B-adapter: the ComponentMapping links need a slug normalize;
  - D: the TSX snippets must parse.
- **Beachball release-scope membership test (C).**
- **Nx implicitDependencies resolve (A by cross_file superset).** I am not sure Nx 22 enforces it; node_modules is absent.
- **@typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment (B-adapter).** Suppression comments block a native rule, as with max-len.
- **Two D units:** `cypress verify`, and the PR website bundle and Storybook build.

**Reclassifications:**
- fluentui-14 goes from A to C. The unstable index.ts allows react-virtualizer additions, so a file digest is stricter than the rule.
- fluentui-31 goes from D to B-adapter (reference), at moderate confidence. For workspace dependencies, incompatible-peer-range reads the committed manifests. It needs a semver-subset operator and an entry-values join. The external-dependency half could be split off as D.

**Removal:** fluentui-11 is an R1 duplicate of fluentui-20. export-maps-sync checks the entry fields and the exports map together, with one message.

**Config:**
- yarnpath-resolves passes silently when the yarnPath key is deleted.
- The entry-fields rule is over-scoped: it includes react-jsx-runtime, which is tagged platform:any.
- The peer-range rule ignores the generator's private-package and protocol-range skips, and its evidence cites the wrong line.
- The LF rule is working-tree based while .gitattributes uses text=auto.
- Every toolchain-pin and dep-version fire claim reproduced. validate-config and check pass on the clone.

**Revised counts:** 77 units: A 20, B 14 (B-adapter 10, B-config 4), C 8, D 35. That gives coverage_today 20/42 = 48%, coverage_with_tuning 28/42 = 67% and gap 14/42 = 33%.

Per family (A/B/C/D):
- toolchain-pin: 4/0/1/1;
- dep-version: 1/4/3/4;
- other: 15/10/4/30.

If fluentui-b16 is not accepted, other A is 14. The scratch directory has been removed and the clone is untouched.

- beachball 3.0.0-alpha.10 internals: whether a missing dependentChangeType is accepted (the rule uses if_present), and whether change files for unknown or private packages only warn.

changes.detail: Stage B config issue reproduced: in scratch, with yarnPath deleted, microsoft-fluentui-yarnpath-resolves stayed silent. Added yaml_path_matches $.yarnPath '^\.yarn/releases/yarn-[^/]+\.cjs$'. It passes on the clone. It fired on yarnPath removed, on yarnPath set to tools/yarn.js and on yarnPath "". Together with yarnpath-resolves it now expresses the A unit.

A toolchain-pin. file_content_forbidden over {.devops/**/*.yml,azure-pipelines*.yml}, pattern (?m)^[^#\n]*\bcorepack\s+enable\b. It passes on the clone; the tools.yml:44 comment does not match. It fired on a `- script: corepack enable` step added to tools.yml (tools.yml:47) and on `corepack enable && yarn generate-version-files` in azure-pipelines.release.yml (:67). Control: a commented '# corepack enable' line did not fire.

The matches pattern changed from ^\S+$ to ^(?s:.*)$, so it accepts any string, like the github-script guard's typeof === 'string' test. It passes on the clone. It fired with syncpack removed. Control: an empty string did not fire (the guard accepts it).
Same change as the syncpack rule (^(?s:.*)$). It passes on the clone. It fired on a numeric value and on beachball moved to dependencies. Control: '^2.0.0 || ^3.0.0' did not fire.

C. The query is now $.peerDependencies[?($.private != true && !match(@, '(workspace|portal|link|file|npm|patch):.*'))]. This mirrors the generator's private-package skip (getSkipReason, index.ts:479-494) and its NON_SEMVER_RANGE skip (index.ts:100, :522). The evidence citation was corrected from :320 (getUnverifiedFloor) to getManifestViolations, index.ts:510-529. It passes on the clone. It fired on react-button peer 'latest' and on '||| 21' with private:false. Controls: 'latest' in a private manifest, and 'npm:react@^18' / 'workspace:*', did not fire.

Added a comment: the regex accepts only exact, ^ and ~ forms, so an in-range '>=2.1.3 <3.0.0' fires. Stage B reproduced this. It is expected for a C range-as-regex, and no fix is possible without a semver operator. The rule is unchanged and passes on the clone.

A other. json_path_matches on change/*.json $.comment, '^(feat|fix|chore|docs|refactor)(\([^)]*\))?!?: \S'. It passes on the clone (12 files). It fired on 'Fixed the focus ring' and on 'perf: faster'. Control: 'feat(react-aria)!: drop x' did not fire.

Stage B removed fluentui-11 as an R1 duplicate of fluentui-20 (B-adapter). The rule is kept at level info as a value-add, with a comment that it partly covers fluentui-20 (the main/module/typings half only, not the exports map). Stage B's scope defect was confirmed by a script over project.json tags: the rule covered 82 manifests against 81 in scope, the extra being react-jsx-runtime (tagged platform:any). It is now excluded, so the rule covers exactly the 81. It passes on the clone. Changing typings on react-button gave an info finding. Control: the same change on react-jsx-runtime gave none.

The pattern is now (?:\A|[^/])(?://[^\S
]*|/\*\s*)tslint ?: ?(?:disable|enable), which mirrors the ESLint rule's comment.value /^\s*tslint .../ test. `///` and `/**` comments no longer match, and line-comment whitespace stays on its line. Its string-literal blindness is documented in a comment. It passes on the clone. It fired on `// tslint:disable` and on a multi-line `/*
 tslint:enable */`. Controls: `/// tslint:disable`, `/** tslint:enable */`, `//* tslint:disable` and `//
tslint:disable` did not fire.

C, following Stage B's reclassification. It replaces the file_hash rule as the unit's rule. It is one anchored file_content_matches over src/unstable/index.ts, generated from the file at the pin, and about 10 KB long. The alert, infobutton, tree and drawer export blocks are pinned name by name, in order. The existing react-virtualizer names must stay, but new names may be inserted in their blocks. Between blocks only comments and further @fluentui/react-virtualizer exports may appear. It passes on the clone. It fired on: a new name in the alert block; a removed alert export; a new export from @fluentui/react-button; a renamed alias (DrawerOverlayProps); and a removed existing virtualizer export (scrollToItemStatic). Controls: a new name inside the virtualizer block, and a new `export { VirtualizerNew } from '@fluentui/react-virtualizer'` at the end of the file, both pass.

Stage A's file_hash on etc/react-components.unstable.api.md, renamed with a va- prefix and set to level info. Its comment says it matches release-cycle.md's literal 'cannot be changed in any way', but it is stricter than the src/unstable/index.ts:4-6 rule (it fires on allowed react-virtualizer additions and on cosmetic api-extractor changes). It passes on the clone. Appending a newline to the report gave an info finding.

No fix is possible. .gitattributes:5 is `*.api.md text=auto` without eol=lf. alint reads the working tree, which is CRLF on a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true, and has no index or blob read. A comment at the rule records the limitation. The rule is unchanged and passes on the Linux clone. See unit_notes.

A other. file_content_matches on AGENTS.md, (?s)<!-- nx configuration start-->.*<!-- nx configuration end-->. It passes on the clone. It fired when the end marker was deleted and when the start marker was reworded.

A other. yaml_path_absent $[?(!$.jobs['copilot-setup-steps'])], used instead of Stage B's runs-on '.+' so that any job content is accepted. It passes on the clone. It fired when the job was renamed to copilot-setup.
A other, using Stage B's yaml_path_matches form on .github/dependabot.yml. It passes on the clone. It fired when the production allow entry was deleted and when it was changed to 'all'.

unit_notes.note: Not fixable inside the clone. .gitattributes:5 is `*.api.md text=auto` with no eol=lf, so Git keeps only the committed blob LF. microsoft-fluentui-api-reports-lf reads the working tree, which is CRLF on a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true, so there the rule fires although the repository content is LF. Keeping A is defensible if the corpus replay is always a Linux clone; the integrator decides.
